What I've done since :

- I've removed TaperedCylinderMesh, as it's not needed
- I've modified CylinderMesh with the following:
  - The icon is that of a tapered cylinder, provided by @MewPurPur 
  - The accessor were top_radius and bottom_radius, in opposition with [the Khronos standard](https://github.com/eoineoineoin/glTF_Physics/blob/master/extensions/2.0/Khronos/KHR_implicit_shapes/schema/glTF.KHR_implicit_shapes.shape.cylinder.schema.json). I've kept those for backward compatibility, but now the "visible" properties are radius_top and radius_bottom.
  - I've added a radius accessor, that gives the means of both radii when read, and sets both radii to the given value when set. This is so that it can be used like a capsule mesh, where only radius exists
- I've modified the TaperedCapsuleMesh to have the same accessors as the CylinderMesh (radius_top, top_radius, radius, bottom_radius, radius_bottom)
- The SVGs from @MewPurPur  have been added where they were meant to be
- I've removed the `#if 0` and commented out code. This was a test to change the way the handles work, from a "distance to line on X" to a "mouse ray is always tangent to radius"
- I've rebased to latest master

Couple of notes:

- The tapered capsule mesh doesn't have handles for the editor gizmo
- The cylinder mesh only has one handle for the radius

I've added the gizmos to the tapered capsule mesh, and moved code from the collision gizmo to the gizmo helper.

The way that the radii are selected is so that the ray from the camera is tangent to a sphere in the case of the capsule, and tangent to a cylinder in the case of the cone. 

This means that when first selecting the gizmo, if the gizmo isn't tangent to the circle, the radius will jump at first, but it also means that if you're aligned with any of the axes, you can still set the radius of the shape. 

In comparison with the cylinder gizmos, the height selection gizmo doesn't change the position of the shape, as there is only one node.

@akien-mga (sorry if this is the wrong way but I saw your comment in the merge queue): I think this is an important addition to godot. The tapered capsule shape is essential for making accurate collision volumes for humanoid ragdolls. When I added it to Jolt, our technical artist where thrilled and now all our ragdolls use it. I would love to see this for 4.7.

Also, TaperedCapsuleMesh should be changed to have the same detail level as CapsuleMesh by default. Right now, it looks like this when viewed from the top with the default parameters (left = TaperedCapsuleMesh, right = CapsuleMesh): To get the same level of detail, **Rings** should either be increased to 16, or its value should be doubled when read in the tapered capsule mesh generation code (and the lowest value allowed should be decreased to `0` to match CapsuleShape). I would prefer the latter personally, as it would ensure the value is set in a consistent manner between CapsuleMesh and TaperedCapsuleMesh. However, it would no longer allow you to have a *slightly* different level of detail between the top and bottom caps, but I don't think it's really needed. Lastly, I noticed TaperedCapsuleMesh exposes a **Height** property in the inspector (the helper for the full height of the mesh), but it's not exposed in the TaperedCapsuleShape3D and TaperedCylinderShape3D inspectors. Could this be done for convenience? CapsuleMesh is also missing a similar helper in the inspector, but it can be done in a separate PR.

Thank you for your effort on this feature. I'm here to share an update.

Project management noticed this is a rather large new feature that has little community interest. This isn't necessarily a disqualification — for example, @fire's and @jrouwe's outspoken support for this are good data points for the value of this PR.
To get a better understanding, we reached out to professional studios, since this is where we thought we might find interest, as professionals tend to need more powerful features than average users. However, none of the studios we are in close contact with have voiced a current need for this feature.

Based on these data, the TLC decided against merging the PR at this point. We'd like to ensure that large new features have a proven community need, and this need hasn't been sufficiently shown yet in the eyes of project management and the TLC.

We'll continue to keep watch on https://github.com/godotengine/godot-proposals/issues/12875. If demand emerges, we'll reconsider a merge of this PR.

Thanks a lot again to @Moddingear and @fire (and everyone else) for your work on this so far — sorry I couldn't bring you better news.

> There is demand, and the reason why I contributed in the first place is because I need this feature, first and foremost, for robotics (where accurate collision is important), and secondly, for a game I was building which needed cones. 

Unfortunately, we cannot merge large features that are needed only by one, or a handful of, people. Being picky about what gets to be in the main engine is a large part of what makes Godot healthy long-term. Keep in mind there are many costs associated with new features, such as maintenance, triage, documentation, tech debt, etc.

> See https://github.com/godotengine/godot-proposals/issues/610, it's much more active. This covers that, as well as 12875.

This is important information that should have been mentioned in the OP. I have amended it in your description.
I'll bring this back to the TLC, but I cannot promise it will change the outcome.

Let me also take this opportunity to explain why I think this is an important change to take. My main interest is in the tapered capsule shape, so let's meet Aloy's ragdoll (from Horizon Zero Dawn, screenshots from Jolt's samples): Her arms and legs are using tapered capsule shapes (note that the bodies should overlap at the knees, they're a bit too far apart in this image). These shapes closely follow the visual mesh of the arm/leg so this shape is a very natural fit. What could you use otherwise: * Capsule shape: This is not a great fit because either it's too narrow at the top or too wide at the bottom of the arm/leg. Both result in the legs penetrating the floor and looking unnatural. Penetration is easiest to spot on arms/legs. * Approximate the arm/leg with several capsule shapes: Possible, but more work to author and more expensive to simulate. * Convex polygon shape: This can be used to approximate the volume of the arm/leg better. Disadvantages are that you need a lot of points to create a round surface (or the shape will not roll properly). It is hard to create them because you need to model a mesh. It costs much more CPU cycles to simulate them. This makes them unsuitable if you want to simulate many ragdolls. That said, if this change is considered too big then I think it could be stripped down: * TaperedCapsuleShape3D: In my opinion, every engine should have this shape. It is a cheap shape that is a good fit for many ragdolls. I think there are plenty of Godot games that need humanoid ragdolls that benefit from this (even if they don't realize this yet). * TaperedCylinderShape3D: Based on the ticket mentioned above, there seems to be interest in this from the community. My opinion is that it is the least stable of all shapes because it has a curved surface meeting a flat plane. This makes it hard to generate a good contact manifold and makes collisions less stable (it works though). I can see use cases for it as a query shape (think directed explosions) and it is useful to fully support the KHR_physics specification. * TaperedCapsuleMesh: Is useful to prototype things using the TaperedCapsuleShape. I think it's unlikely that anything will ship using it so it could be cut. Then there could be the argument that this is the first feature that is not supported by Godot Physics. I think we're slowly deprecating Godot Physics, but if that's important then I could take a look at implementing the tapered capsule shape (if there is commitment that this will be merged).
If there's no drawback to it then maybe tapering could just be added to the base CapsuleMesh instead of making a separate resource, like how CylinderMesh has tapering built-in.

I will also add that we need tapered capsules and tapered cylinders for glTF compatibility.

Khronos has decided that these shapes are important and are expected to be implemented in every engine.

I am likely going to be using these shapes for some terrain in my game. I think it has more uses than people think, its just that no one initally thinks "lets request a new feature" for an issue they have when there is probably an at most slightly worse alternative, such as (in the tapered capsule scenario) a trimesh collision in the shape of a tapered capsule. But if X feature is added, more people think of it and therefore more people would use it than the set of people on github who specifically thought that this was a good solution to their problem even though it has not been added yet.
also, some people would use a feature and just aren't vocal about it.
Point is, just because Y number of people ask for a feature, it doesn't always mean that exactly Y, or even slightly more or less, people will use it.
Idk what i am saying really. I'm mostly just wondering what is going on with this PR now.

From my point of view: this is one of the many many features that a _user_ of godot would expect to exist, and when it doesn't the immediate resolution is: "well I'll work around this bullshit then". So then very simple features will just become PRs that have been sitting around for years due to "little community interest" - when actually what happens is "well that's inconvenient but workaroundable". It seems that most of the PR decisions on the godot engine are not made by actual users of the engine.

Your shows of support for this feature is appreciated and helps triage this. However, I should note that the PR comment section is not the place to do it. Instead, please direct this to the proposals (support existing ones, or open new ones). 

This is how we (the maintainers), and the TLC, judge user demand. The previous TLC decision was hinged largely on the fact that very little user demand was shown (at the time: one proposal description linked with 5 upvotes, and two shows of support from maintainers). An update will be posted when the TLC has reconvened.

Hi folks, 

We rediscussed in the TLC in light of https://github.com/godotengine/godot-proposals/issues/610 (which we weren't aware of during the last discussion). 

https://github.com/godotengine/godot-proposals/issues/610 shows that there is indeed a high level of demand for tapered cylinder collision shapes which resolves our main concern about going ahead with this. Our main concern was that there was relatively no demand from people making games. 

The other concern was whether it is okay to support certain shapes in Jolt physics, but not in Godot physics. And, if so, what should happen (i.e. should we fallback to non-tapered cylinders/capsules, should we provide a warning and suggest switching to Jolt physics, or should we fallback to convex colliders?). 

Overall the TLC has agreed that we are okay with Jolt being the priority for development and new features and letting Godot physics fall behind to an extent. This decision comes from the fact that Godot physics simply doesn't have a maintainer and we feel that it can't be fully maintained with our current resources. 

Overall, the results of the discussion are that we are now okay with merging this PR. We may need to add a warning in Godot physics, but that can be done in a follow up PR if the automatic fallback indeed causes confusion. 

Thank you everyone for providing your input and thank you to Moddingear for your work!
There's no need for a fallback in Godot physics. A warning and/or error on use is fine, ideally with UI affordances to warn early.

Since it came up in chat, a clarification: The TLC has _not_ code-reviewed the PR. The decision that was made was that the proposed feature can be added to the engine (jolt-only). 

The PR is still up for (and might need) further code review.

- This needs to be merged with the existing shape and mesh types by adding new properties to not cause so much Resource type inflation.

- The added new properties need to by default be disabled.

- This needs a bool-like way for users / parsers / servers to enable and detect the new feature to branch to optimized paths as tapered has a noticeable performance cost.

- The physics tapered shapes need efficient triangle creation for geometry parsers. The current geometry works with a Mesh and creates 90%+ array data that a parser does not need, slowing everything down.

- All the shape and mesh related parsers in the engine need to be updated. E.g. Navmesh parsers in StaticBody and GridMap or the Editor importers.

> This needs to be merged with the existing shape and mesh types by adding new properties to not cause so much Resource type inflation.
> The added new properties need to by default be disabled.
> This needs a bool-like way for users / parsers / servers to enable and detect the new feature to branch to optimized paths as tapered has a noticeable performance cost.

So, if I understand correctly, you want the new tapered shapes to become an option in the old non-tapered shapes ?

> The physics tapered shapes need efficient triangle creation for geometry parsers. The current geometry works with a Mesh and creates 90%+ array data that a parser does not need, slowing everything down.
> All the shape and mesh related parsers in the engine need to be updated. E.g. Navmesh parsers in StaticBody and GridMap or the Editor importers.

This implementation isn't using triangle meshes. This is simple collision. Godot physics don't have that and as such, the fallback is the non-tapered shapes.

> you want the new tapered shapes to become an option in the old non-tapered shapes ?

yes. tapered and the handful of required new properties can be added to the related existing types. the servers can handle and branch internally to more optimized paths when they have a way to know if tapered is used or not.

> This implementation isn't using triangle meshes. This is simple collision. Godot physics don't have that and as such, the fallback is the non-tapered shapes.

For physics alone yes but shapes are Resources not just used by physics. They are used for plenty of geometry related functionality and for that regularly need a way to convert to triangle arrays. When adding the tapered functionality to the existing related Mesh types can just update the Mesh::create_mesh_array() functions as that is what nearly all the existing parsers already use.

> yes. tapered and the handful of required new properties can be added to the related existing types. the servers can handle and branch internally to more optimized paths when they have a way to know if tapered is used or not.

The issue I see with that is one of migration, the current capsules use radius and height, but tapered capsules use top/bottom radius and mid_height, same for cylinders. Is there a way for the update to not break stuff ?

> For physics alone yes but shapes are Resources not just used by physics. They are used for plenty of geometry related functionality and for that regularly need a way to convert to triangle arrays. When adding the tapered functionality to the existing related Mesh types can just update the Mesh::create_mesh_array() functions as that is what nearly all the existing parsers already use.

That's already done. TaperedCapsuleMesh overloads Mesh::create_mesh_array() and is used by TaperedCapsuleShape. TaperedCylinderShape uses the mesh generated in CylinderMesh, as that already supports tapering.

I could rename TaperedCapsuleMesh to CapsuleMesh and delete the old CapsuleMesh, and that would accomplish what you're asking, unless i'm missing something ?

> The issue I see with that is one of migration, the current capsules use radius and height, but tapered capsules use top/bottom radius and mid_height, same for cylinders. Is there a way for the update to not break stuff ?

You could add a `tapered_enabled` bool on the shape/mesh that toggles the new properties for tapered in the inspector to avoid the user interface clutter and have an easy way to detect if a geometry is used as tapered or not.

Then add those tapered specific properties that can not be shared / reused from the normal version as extra properties to the Resource. E.g. in case of cylinders add `top_radius` and `bottom_radius` but keep the `height` as `height`. When a user toggles the tapered_enabled on and off all that visibly should change is the tapered part of the shape but the height should stay the same no matter how it is internally calculated.

Assuming we have such a tapered bool to detect, you can update the Mesh::create_mesh_array() code of the related mesh primitives and branch internal so that it creates the old version or the new tapered version depending on what is used. That way you dont need to bother updating each parser tool individual as they will just get whatever version is set.


To sum up.
- add properties to existing, related shapes and mesh primitives with a toggle `tapered_enabled` and keep tapered default disabled.
- Reuse existing properties that make sense, add new when required. Keep the overall shape size the same when toggled, see height example above.
- update any geometry functions of those existing resources to handle `tapered_enabled`.
E.g.
`Shape3D::get_debug_mesh_lines()`
`Shape3D::get_debug_arraymesh_faces()`
`Mesh::create_mesh_array()`
...
- update server internals to branch between normal and tapered
when it matters like for jolt, in case of unsupported like GodotPhysics3D throw the warning if tapered is used
- update documentation and documentation images yada-yada
You can join dev chat and documentation channel if you need help with any of that and/or poke skyace65 for doc specifically.

I've had to rework the way gizmo handles work so that the gizmos can allow switching between tapered and non-tapered. 
This implementation removes the translation on the gizmo for the height handles.

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/3dc98ad9-5f8d-4668-ab58-306154183911

Non-tapered shapes support being represented by tapered shapes, and vice-versa (though, when a tapered shape is represented by a non-tapered shape, the collision doesn't match ofc).

It now uses non-tapered shapes when top_radius and bottom_radius are the same.

There is an accessor for radius, which sets both top_radius and bottom_radius to the same value, and when read, gives the average of both.

Tapered shapes have 6 longitudinal lines, as opposed to non-tapered shapes which have 4, so they can easily be told apart.

I haven't tested migrating cylinder shapes from 4.7 to this version.

The shape resources with the new tapered properties combined look mostly fine. Combining that tapered feature with existing shape types implied doing it on the PhysicsServer API and extension layer as well.

Right now those server and extension files have extra entries in enums and functions that should not exist. It should not concern the user at the server API level if they use e.g. a normal capsule or a tapered capsule, it is all just capsule with some extra tapered properties.

Now there are valid reason to handle them different (mostly performance) but that is something the physics engine backend can and should internally branch to more optimized paths if it detects certain properties in use. It is not a concern of the front server API to do this technical split.

So `virtual RID tapered_capsule_shape_create() = 0;` and `virtual RID tapered_cylinder_shape_create() = 0;` and everything related should be removed and wrapped into the existing and only branches if necessary on the internals of the module code, aka inside GodotPhysics or Jolt.

The only place you need to send geometry data is with the `shape_set_data()` and that is a `Variant` that is a `Dictionary` for the shapes with more than one property.

So you can add key-value pairs for tapered related properties when tapered is enabled and used on that shape and leave them out when not. Everything else is up to the physics backend and does not concern the core physics server directly, e.g. falling back to the simpler default shape when the tapered keys are not found in the dict.

On creation of e.g. a capsule shape all that is happening (or should) is a request for a  `RID` handle in the shape rid pool that sets the type to e.g. capsule shape. The shape has no real data at that point (outside some almost useless default values) and it does not know what it really wants to be until the first `shape_set_data()` call that defines the actual shape geometry.

The way to avoid this change of properties and magic radius calculation that will create compatibility problems and make users trip is to add the `tapered_enabled` toggle that we talked about early.

One thing that will change between 4.7 and this, is that setting height then radius isn't the same as setting radius then height, since it's going though mid_height.
Setting height then radius isn't the same as setting radius then height. That behavior gives the impression of a bug.

It's not a bug.

It's a different implementation.

Example with a capsule that starts at radius 1 and height 2:
- in the old version, height is 2.
- in the new version, mid_height is 0

Let's set height to 3, then radius to 0.5:
- in the old version, height is set the 3, radius is set to 0.5. this works.
- in the new version, mid_height is set to 1, then radius is set to 0.5. height becomes 2.
- doing the opposite (radius then height) in the new version, height changes temporarily to 1 then 3.

Old version conserved height.

New version conserves mid_height.

If height is important, it should be set after radius.

> If height is important, it should be set after radius.

The addition of an order constraint here is going to break scripts and maybe even some content. Some games that dynamically create capsule shapes are going to start getting different physics and the devs are possibly going to have no idea why their games broke.

we *could* make a huge deal about it in patch notes "check your scripts to make sure you set height second!!!", but do devs all read those?

creating capsule shapes in script is common for player controllers setting up a CharacterBody3D and incorrect height values could cause players to clip into the floor or fall through the level.

In my opinion,  this change could use one of these two approaches to avoid breaking compatibility on game scripts that create a new capsule shape then set height -> radius

### Idea 1. Implicit mode

You could put it into a height preserving mode depending on if you most recently explicitly set height or mid_height.

if you set_height, it sets height preserving to true and then set_radius will recalculate mid_height after.

If set_mid_height is called, it would clear height preserving mode.

### idea 2. Explicit mode dropdown/checkbox

for a more godot way to do this, make an enum (dropdown) or checkbox for how height is set, defaulting to height for compatibility

Both height and mid_height have default usage in the ADD_PROPERTY line. based on the checkbox, the other property is set in _validate_property to PROPERTY_USAGE_NONE.

finally, we'd need to actually store both height and mid_height, and the code in set_height and set_mid_height will set the other property based on the mode value, so for example, if it's set to height mode, set_mid_height will bring back the old calculation for height (but based on top radius + bottom radius instead of 2*radius)

@lyuma I've implemented it in Explicit mode.

Setting the height below the minimum afforded by the radii shrinks them.

Setting the radii above height/2 increases height.

When Use height is on, only Height is saved. When it's off, only mid_height is saved. It's on by default.
